headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: unstructured can write and egress by default while awesome-nlp is non-runnable and networkless, making prompt-injection and leakage mostly low but interaction safety still needs isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces and no network egress, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can read files and process documents, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel beyond manual transfer. That makes prompt injection possible mainly through unusual copy-paste or file handoff, not default interaction.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A-facing prompts or files
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or clipboard outside the profiles
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid copy-pasting B outputs into A prompts
Use a one-way export format with no instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred files

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not a leakage source. B reads documents/images/text and can write files, but its network egress is allowlisted and the profiles do not show shared storage or sensitive data classes. Leakage is therefore limited to an unusual shared-workspace setup.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace or directory
IF sensitive documents are placed in B-readable paths and then exported from B
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Restrict B to non-sensitive sample documents
Disable outbound network for B during tests
Review allowlisted endpoints before processing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has write_filesystem, read_filesystem, subprocess, and package-install capabilities, while A is non-runnable and exposes no write surface. There is no direct write-write conflict with A, but B’s mutable filesystem and concurrent-instance support can still collide with operator-managed files or shared artifacts if the pair is co-located.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF B instances run concurrently against shared mutable files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate output directory
Run only one B instance per workspace
Lock shared files before writes
Use read-only mounts for A inputs
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume files and produce downstream outputs, so if A’s content is manually fed into B, B may treat it as input without a verification layer. A itself is not runnable, which reduces direct chaining, but the pair still supports a human-mediated pipeline where unverified text can cascade into document-processing outputs.
conditions: IF A-generated text is copied into B as source material
IF B outputs are used downstream without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output
Mark A output as untrusted in filenames
Compare B output against source documents
Keep A and B in separate stages
requires-engineering: add validation checksums between stages

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU residency, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. A touches no data classes and B touches documents/images/text with allowlisted egress, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy mismatch rather than a specific residency or regulated-data violation. The other agent is cited because the pairwise flow is still relevant.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed through B
IF the operator relies on undocumented retention or residency guarantees
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair
Confirm retention settings before use
Review B privacy policy and docs
Store outputs in the required region
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
